citation: H. J. Liu, Q. B. Sun, N. Huang, J. Wen, Z. L. Wang, "Highly efficient pulse cleaner via nonlinear ellipse rotation in liquid CS2 for ultrashort pulses", Opt. Lett. 38(11), 1838-1840 (2013)
fullTextRead: Yes: the licensed PDF (3 pages) was read through its text layer (PyMuPDF; the Read tool's PDF mode needs pdftoppm, which is not installed) and the equations and figures through rendered page images. Eq. (1) and the n2 value were checked on a rendered crop. Figure values are read off the plots. The PDF is not in the repository.
topic: temporal-contrast enhancement by nonlinear ellipse rotation: QWP, CS2 Kerr cell, perpendicular QWP, crossed polariser

referenceNumbers.value: I_NER = I_in sin^2(2 alpha) sin^2(phi_SPM cos(2 alpha)/6)
input contrast 1e5, 800 nm, 100 fs Gaussian; transmissivity maximum > 60 % at alpha ~ 34 deg
T(phi_SPM) rises to ~0.65-0.7 near phi = 9-10 pi (alpha = 34 deg), axis 0-12 pi
contrast improved by four orders of magnitude when the polariser-analyser extinction ratio is better than 1e4
n2 = (3 +- 0.6)e-19 m2/W; breakdown 2e13 W/cm2; response 70 fs (refs 12-14)
808 nm, 70 fs, spectrum 20 nm; two achromatic zero-order QWPs; f = 500 mm lenses; 2 mm quartz cell of CS2 at the focus; polarising splitter ER > 1e4
optimal alpha 32.5 deg (xi = tan alpha) for the highest transmissivity
>30 % at 6 mJ and ~320 GW/cm2 (lower than theory: optics losses and quality)
contrast enhanced ~3 orders of magnitude (limited by scatter, ER, waveplate accuracy)
cleaned pulse ~60 fs FWHM, narrower than the 70 fs input, not distorted

assumptions: The paper-model runs use a user material: index = Kedenburg et al., Opt. Mater. Express 2, 1588 (2012), n^2 = 1 + 1.50387 l^2/(l^2 - 0.03049) (l in um, 20 C, 0.5-1.6 um) as published on refractiveindex.info (CC0); not from the paper and not cross-checked against a second source. GDD at 808 nm from it: 218 fs2/mm. Since 2026-11 the engine's built-in material CS2 has the same index (checked: identical result in the Shimizu replication).

n2 = 3e-19 m2/W (the paper's value) as an instantaneous Kerr effect, which is what Eq. (1) assumes. The paper cites a 70 fs response but no delayed part. A sensitivity run uses the built-in CS2 (electronic 3e-19 plus a delayed orientational part, total 3e-18, 0.2/1.6 ps, anisotropicFraction 1.5; all UNVERIFIED typical values) on a 40 ps window; it is not a claim about the paper.
1-D plane wave. The experiment is a focused beam (P/Pcr ~ 4e5 at 6 mJ, 70 fs); self-focusing and the beam size in the cell are not modelled and not given.

Eq. (1) is reproduced only if the angle is measured from the other waveplate axis, alpha_paper = 45 deg - alpha_fast-axis, and phi_SPM = 2 B(linear) (derived with Jones calculus, see README), not with the paper's literal definitions.
Waveplates and polariser are ideal (achromatic, retardance exactly lambda/4); the experiment's 99 % purity and optics losses are not modelled, so the measured 30 % is not a check.
320 GW/cm2 is taken as the peak intensity of linear light in the cell; the paper does not say which plane or which definition.
